subject: I just finished a long day of knocking on doors

body:
Our end-of-month deadline is just hours away.
Hi Peter, it's Pramila.
I just finished a long day of knocking on doors here in Seattle! I am so inspired by all the volunteers who turned out to help support not only my campaign, but progressive candidates up and down the ballot.
But we won't let up until the polls close. This election is too important to leave to chance, and I'm counting on you to help us cross the finish line.
With our end-of-month deadline just hours away, will you chip in at the link below to help us fund our final efforts to get out the vote?
[**https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pj-em-20261031-2**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20261031-2.PCLBQn&refcode=em20261031-6908&t=1&akid=6908%2E420207%2EO9t3kc)
Thank you, thank you, thank you for your support.
— PJ

It's the last night of October and just hours from our end of month deadline.
I'm the only Democratic Senator up for reelection in a state Trump won in 2024. And MAGA has spent tens of millions to flip this seat.
Before you turn in: **[Can you rush $10 before midnight to help me win in Georgia?](https://substack.com/redirect/e9d92f9a-4bab-48c0-bfc0-701209184b31?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

When I first ran for Senate six years ago, it was because I believed the election of someone so deeply unfit for the presidency posed a danger to the country.
Many people said it couldn't be done. But you believed -- not just in me, but in the idea that Georgia could lead, and that our Republic is worth defending.
Then we won. Not just a Senate seat, but the Senate majority for Democrats.
Now Trump has launched a power grab unprecedented in our history, abusing his power and trying to poison our Republic with fear and intimidation.
Americans are now living in fear of their own government.
I'm fighting back.
And I need you with me.

Case File No DRT-ED-AUSTIN · Special File · The Austin Lab
Apple Says American Factories Were On Track to Make More Than 19 Billion Chips for Its Products in 2025. Most iPhone Owners Have No Idea Where They Come From.
In August 2025, Apple raised its U.S. investment pledge to $600 billion and named partners building chips for the iPhone on American soil. Austin, Texas, sits close to the middle of that effort. The parts inside your phone have quietly become a national priority.
Threat level 3/5 — Guarded

Most people know who designs the iPhone. Almost nobody knows who makes the dozens of chips inside it. Those suppliers rarely make headlines, yet each one can collect a share of every phone sold. And as Washington pushes chipmaking back to America, some of them are getting a bigger role.
The evidence board
| | What We Know
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — the pledge.** On August 6, 2025, Apple raised its U.S. commitment to $600 billion over four years and launched its American Manufacturing Program.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit B — Austin.** Apple said it’s working with Samsung at its Austin chip plant on a manufacturing technology never used before anywhere in the world, to supply chips for iPhones sold worldwide.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the scale.** Apple said the U.S. silicon supply chain was on track to produce more than 19 billion chips for its products in 2025.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit D — the campus.** Apple’s second Austin campus is expanding, with three more buildings under construction, including a research lab for hardware and software teams.
| OUR THEORY
---
When the world’s most valuable phone maker moves its supply chain home, the small suppliers behind it can become much more important, and much more valuable.

Turn off the lights. Lock the doors. Check under the bed, Fellow Patriot.

Because tonight, on Halloween, something truly terrifying is creeping toward South Carolina.

It isn't a ghost. It isn't a ghoul. **It's Annie Andrews, and she's been feeding on $25 MILLION in liberal cash to grow stronger.**

In just three days, she could crawl out of the shadows and into the U.S. Senate.

And if she does, here's the horror that follows her home:

[](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=3932ea170e87421ab7a40d9ac55d1273&_e=iOLBrK43Um7VOJiGCRBa8gvNvuXWqtBj-39C6gaBJmM4fxRlgH_oo16rsbGqdA1y9wVXl0u8hh3JELHoQucBx8gxeoFH-Qb-mu8YPDU3VMaZeJOTmX9-iBEQ2JN2ZsLwjgRcN2XwpyCFMEzRg6L14Lsg41nWQxgUPMeqP6hTAsjT2dW7SqXGgxrk4qjism0ouswBcuamQwGt5uD8CwE8aF-ds4YZL5eiHrqxCYnXKW0vJccbGrLcSIKkc88xldDrzz5Oo10_EJBe4hsjoSdTYIIs7PuDPJFw3Oicy6M7WWmgaJc1Ntwhu35fRrNXBddGlLh4PriB7Xp_CMTtroZ7KmiB_8cP2HviP1L9mLDJmmOB8W0nTurrDPGueKOgpW8KWwLIhnN4tPv1_TkHb2oYCyFBZ2XHVFX1rQ1D3H6Bnf43-jhfQqJXfeI2-yyfPgYOLFXX3Hvfz7U1QEna80A5hTAkGP7s-7KFFCuXYvc_6mG1aWtTYJDl6SsUSXxdWN0cwewdNgQTu4swU8NlulypM--M085hR2O5jsLhBWyX0ZS7Zet-fBnnp8V_yqjWODtN-gTKHBVWehClT9Mh4hyCaB5xMhW95m9vI_zfKW3sS_gPOivCO8dgWYDP7gzVd_ErcazvKl1pdzrtmiktLQUDatuZ606f5-UYv8iBgFKg7FJOgIwDa53GDB-bn_qui-iKUoX5D0L7qyYv7x6PPLbZ7mxxBR3zXnFAw7jlscibr-8%3D)
This isn't a haunted house you can walk out of. _There's no exit sign_. **If Annie Andrews wins, this nightmare lasts six long years.**

She is the most radical Democrat ever nominated statewide in South Carolina, and the Radical Left has poured $25 million into her campaign because they know exactly what she'll do with that Senate seat.

Only one person stands between South Carolina and this horror story: **Darline Graham.**

# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=2234%2E1086043%2EJHAoPr)
Hi Peter, it’s Lieutenant Governor Aruna Miller.
**_Leave No One Behind._**
Those are the first words you see when you drive into Maryland, and they're the promise Wes and I made to every Marylander on day one of taking office.
Together, we've made real progress. We accelerated the path to a $15 minimum wage. We've sent more than $200 million in utility rebates to families struggling with energy costs. Violent crime is dropping, our economy is stronger, and our public schools are getting better.
But the job's not done.
**Election Day is just 2 days away, Peter.** Dan Cox and his MAGA allies are spending millions in attack ads to flip the governorship and take Maryland backward.
We can’t let that happen — and we’re counting on your support to fight back.
**[Will you chip in $5 or any amount right now to help us finish the job and keep building a Maryland that leaves no one behind?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261101-1.7SDqKI&refcode=em-20261101-1&t=2&akid=2234%2E1086043%2EJHAoPr)**

With gratitude,
Aruna Miller

name: Kylie Glatfelter
subject: Nieshalla: Indiana’s Financial Turnaround Success Story
body:
No images? [Click here](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-e-fhkpyk-hhlljjcji-o/)
# **Nieshalla: Indiana 's Financial Turnaround Success Story**
By Indiana State Comptroller Elise NieshallaIndiana has a financial turnaround story to remember - I dare say, on par with the remarkable transformation of Indiana University football. We've gone from headlines twenty-plus years ago like "Indiana's financial hole is staggering" by the Indiana Fiscal Policy Institute to more recent ones like "[Balanced budget amendment passes](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fhkpyk-hhlljjcji-r/)" and "[Indiana's state budget reserves jump 60% in past year to $4B](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fhkpyk-hhlljjcji-y/)."In fact, in 2002, when Democrats were at the helm, Indiana closed its books with only six cents in General Fund reserves, and our total reserve funds were spent down by 74% while hundreds of millions of dollars in payments to our schools were delayed.Just as the IU Hoosiers went from losing the most games in college football history to becoming champions, we've gone from closing our books "in the black" by six cents to having a balanced budget amendment in our Indiana Constitution that is the gold standard for the states. As I like to say, we've gone from **_six cents to common sense._** In addition, the State of Indiana has gone from being in the bottom half of the _Rich States, Poor States_ ranking by the American Legislative Exchange Council to now being in the top ten. We also have the fourth-lowest debt per capita among the states, along with growth rates for population and GDP that outpace all our neighboring states.Even the Chicago Bears have come to see Indiana as the land of milk and honey.When Governor Mitch Daniels and a Republican-led legislature came on the scene in 2004, they got to work turning our State around financially. Due to the fiscal transformation they were able to accomplish, the State of Indiana started running a clever ad campaign to lure businesses from Illinois and California to the great Hoosier State -- and the message, "Admit it, you find me fiscally attractive," was compelling then, and is even more so today.Now after two decades of Republican leadership prioritizing fiscal responsibility, discipline and transparency, Indiana's financial transformation is a true success story of a state that's been put back on financial high ground with balanced budgets, healthy reserves, low debt, well-funded pensions, and a AAA credit rating.Furthermore, the Indiana General Assembly has lowered the individual income tax rate from 3.4% to 2.95%, and it will reach a new low next year of 2.9%. All the while, our tax base and revenues have grown, giving us the ability to implement a Gas Tax Holiday when Hoosiers needed relief the most -- and still reimburse revenue to counties, cities and towns to make their transportation budgets whole. In addition, Indiana is on track to achieve fully-funded status a decade ahead of schedule for the once-struggling Pre-96 Teacher Pension Fund -- and we have paid cash for capital projects and issued two taxpayer refunds.To top it off, we are leading the way in bringing the bright light of transparency to federal dollars coming to Indiana through the newly launched Federal Funding Expenditures Dashboard or "The FEDD" -- a phenomenal new tool to help state agencies, our U.S. District Attorneys, the FBI, the DOJ, the media and public expose fraud. We are an open book, and sunlight is the best disinfectant.While we often point out how Indiana's financial health is leaps and bounds ahead of Illinois' -- our debt per capita is $169 while theirs is $2,332 -- we hope our fiscal success serves as an inspiration to them and other struggling states, like IU's football program is to other colleges across the country.It is now our responsibility to keep Indiana financially strong and stable as the bright star of the Midwest and beyond.Indiana has done the hard work to turn itself around, and may we be an inspiration to our beloved country that is facing the tremendous challenge of being $40 trillion in debt.As Hoosiers, we now also need to help build a movement to turn around our country's finances and **_Make America Like Indiana._** This election, Republicans ask for your vote to continue advancing fiscal responsibility, discipline and transparency for our great State. Let's do our utmost to keep Indiana strong. [](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fhkpyk-hhlljjcji-j/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fhkpyk-hhlljjcji-t/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fhkpyk-hhlljjcji-i/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fhkpyk-hhlljjcji-d/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fhkpyk-hhlljjcji-h/) | [Unsubscribe](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-u-fhkpyk-hhlljjcji-b/)
---

Dear Patriot,

Right now, in campaign offices across this country, people are looking at the new volunteer a little differently, and
https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNDcsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA91DMWlFcs3Vm5Lq5bY20KJLTa08YUAvQ0HwScNud3NYP_Gev9XVqvynVsSNSHnCQHc4KNs8lFvuVRPUyM2R-iBhwE6zKgR_tiid9bWunA
that's exactly why I need you with me.

Two weeks ago, I posted a warning to every midterm campaign in America: “We have undercover people inside midterm campaigns across the United States.” And I told them:
“I'm watching every single thing you ALL are doing.”

714,000 people saw that post. The campaigns saw it too. Then Detroit came out, and a man who swore he could spot one of us from across the room learned that he had been talking to one of my journalists all along.

So what's on the other tapes? I can't tell you yet, and I want you to understand exactly why, because the reason is the same thing that made Detroit hold up the moment it went public.

I said in that same post that we would not release footage until we had checked the facts, corroborated our sources and gotten comment, so that every story was absolutely bulletproof. That promise is the most expensive part of what we do. It means editors reviewing every hour of raw footage, researchers checking every claim against the public record, and calls to every person on tape to give them a chance to explain. Then the lawyers read every word.
https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNDcsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA91DMWlGUX_9Wm4XqPtiRP1WxDMSe4VhQ3pvIKDQfeR4_PommydOVHQFTNYrsZFikr-dcHhjRsqJjBqvpCK_pWPc3vVSnTSz8f5H5ulkwQ
Help me keep that promise.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNDcsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA91DMWlHbWVNl_J-6I1ty-_M0leQrWtb6_6ls6m0qu28qLkBYHwPAwHEXa8yXbzsrQhMnDGSdR5NTnr0yMnFVnKmuVZjSdOSazSn_TUVNw

It also means I won't rush. If a story is ready before Tuesday, you'll see it. If it needs one more source, it waits. I would rather be right than first, because when the denials come, and they always come, our story has to be the one still standing.

Detroit showed what happens when we do it right: a campaign statement, a party statement and a staffer who is no longer employed. The next one will be held to the same standard.
https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNDcsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA91DMWlIbChhiRiMmeYjRaMh2AUfzoVmmDY5kwwpmoOfoKq1LqzOWFhGPxBsUoiEgias0EvTCNCmMVO_AczoANfWOTDRwTYR22yxEf2lAw
Help me get it out the door.

Covering the $47,000 we spent on Detroit is what lets my team stay focused on the next release instead of the last bill. We have two days left.

subject: Two days
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Small Town PAC, [smalltownpac
body:
Small Town PAC is making sure our slate has what they need to win.
#
It’s now or never, Peter.
As I write this, _Election Day is just two days away._ That leaves no room for error, but we have a plan to win on Tuesday.
Small Town PAC is backing a strong slate of nine Democratic candidates running for Congress and governor across the country. I’ve run plenty of tough races myself, and **I know there’s only one surefire way to make sure they come out on top: actually getting out and talking to voters.**
There’s nothing like a good face-to-face conversation. Not only does it give you the chance to address people’s concerns directly, but it also helps us rebuild the sense of community that’s been fractured by this divisive administration in Washington.
If our candidates like Amy Acton in Ohio and Jake Johnson in Minnesota are going to win, we have to make sure their teams reach as many voters as possible before polls close on Tuesday.
Doing that kind of voter contact the right way isn’t cheap. Organizing last-minute canvasses and phone banks takes resources — and Small Town PAC is making sure they have what they need to pull them off.
If we don’t back them now, our slate could fall short and lose. It’s as simple as that.
**[Peter, can you chip in $5 to make sure our slate of Democratic fighters for the working class can reach enough voters to win in two days?](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261101-1._OARW_&amount=5&refcode=em20261030-1296&t=1&akid=1296%2E34582%2EVJbOkd)**

Tim Walz

name: Voto Latino
subject: Thank you, Peter.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Voto Latino
body:
1.6 million voters. 22 districts. 6 states. 2 days.
#
Peter,
**We’re just two days away from Election Day, and we want to take a moment to thank you.**
All cycle long, we’ve been sending you updates on our work, and at the same time, your support has been out in the field doing that work: reaching Latino voters in the states and districts that will decide this election. Every text sent, every call made, and every voter who learned where, when, and how to cast their ballot was made possible by people like you.
Here’s where that work is happening right now. We’re on the ground in Arizona, Nevada, North Carolina, Georgia, Pennsylvania, and Texas, and across 22 target congressional districts from coast to coast. In many of these districts, Latino voters make up the margin between winning and losing, and the races could be decided by just a few thousand votes.
That’s why these final two days are so important.
The voters we still need to reach are often the ones who’ve been overlooked the longest: new voters, young voters, and people who’ve been told their voice doesn’t count. A personal text or a phone call from a trusted messenger can be the difference between staying home and showing up. **That’s why we’re going all in, but we’re going to need a final surge of support to help get these races across the finish line.**
**[We can’t do it without you, Peter. Will you chip in $3 or any amount to help us reach Latino voters in this final stretch?](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20261101-1.TNzvAr&amount=3&refcode=em20261101-741&t=1&akid=741%2E1366028%2EeEGMUV)**

| | November 1, 2026
Lamont, Blanchard and Hughes Incidents Show Their Disdain for the Law
* Don't get in the way of their 'will to power'

In the space of just 12 hours, as this last weekend of campaigning commenced, it was revealed that each of these Democrat candidates' arrogant actions got themselves tangled up with the law.
On Friday, a report made its way into the press that the prior week, Rob Blanchard, candidate for District 28 senate seat for Fairfield, Newtown, Bethel and Easton, was cited for disobeying a patrol officer's instructions for avoiding a road construction site and crashed his car. Blanchard is also Ned Lamont's communications director, as he runs for elective office. Details finally appeared in the Newtown Bee - see [Blanchard](https://lk9rohfbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001LOZngNu9RwkwEFmlHWv5qph_1153tXjT6dp7UaIVB80Td5YJHTyt_xJ5ZCZXN91uYrT1FtcFrDZYz21ig60w5xELmJxmE4CdOdhIBR6NQ6npi8i1qSlugX1pCdJtURrFtsryRYUN9ppPeXWeUjTdYJYODpziJ0LpXApAyKswN9MnRF_6yTsX7yqwxaqj5E6EAldmYJcKc2V3WMVikXwOE2eC5DUxXBUkzMv70x3znOeEnuaV13EV3ww2fZxCmMkTNpbYE8Fq-mhqttkLfhCKAMUUifmFRkR5DdFyd1bLwFWgy_3zX5sfQi3q8MeyCLfzNZfaMNms9eg=&c=3PCmBSOPF8aR-yNeBMg7pXWZ2pENxCZiyFWmUN2EKxpTJv9m13pMuA==&ch=SaYDp5FnPNPkJaMG6avjolj_rWBrkXPuGz0oSlWELxulK5FEsd72lA==).
As the man in a hurry disregarded police instruction, his front wheel collapsed into a hole and disabled his car. Funny how it took a week for this to make its way to print.
Then Blanchard's comrade, Easton incumbent Democrat State Rep Anne Hughes was arrested Friday night for stealing the campaign signs of her opponent, Republican Darrell Harris, and stashing them in her garage. Turns out team Harris was tired of getting their signs stolen, so they 'air-tagged' a few and Hughes scarfed them up in the dead of night, and the police came tracking and calling. See [Hughes Article](https://lk9rohfbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001LOZngNu9RwkwEFmlHWv5qph_1153tXjT6dp7UaIVB80Td5YJHTyt_xJ5ZCZXN91ueViG-haxk8usB7F_BqpqVM-tyJtb6heUdYwW-DQ3S8hNMBOntomgt9cBtJUThOjJj2AZ0yde1TmBN3gdDMqZLhT2W3XIjVtXUjeLVHrBEN3321KdzkApuMRov2bLSTDZTJptQyvEXeurTee7ON8IL0lBabIWq0QV4_yfe2-y5eWBZl75CodggGnkVy2EuetP81zvzVA8PIlMPPDFS6eebU9e-FQZEBl_&c=3PCmBSOPF8aR-yNeBMg7pXWZ2pENxCZiyFWmUN2EKxpTJv9m13pMuA==&ch=SaYDp5FnPNPkJaMG6avjolj_rWBrkXPuGz0oSlWELxulK5FEsd72lA==)
Evidently, Hughes feels she MUST get reelected to continue controlling the lives of the citizens of District 135, and can't let a freedom-loving Republican get in her way.
And birds of a feather, Blanchard and Hughes, are such best-buds that they launched their campaigns together. Here's the poster announcing their campaign canvassing kickoff.
---
|
---
Not to be outdone, our nervous governor let his disdain toward independent press show on Saturday when he smacked away a reporter's camera when she asked for a comment on his communication director's (Blanchard) run-in with the Newtown police. (I've seen capitol police detain someone for tapping a Rep's shoulder on the floor of the LOB in Hartford) Directly below is the video Jackie Homan of The Connecticut Centinal was shooting when Lamont got 'spooked' by an uncomfortable inquiry as he arrived for an otherwise controlled event in Stamford.

subject: These 10 judges are building an oligarchy.
disclaimer_text: paid for by the right-wing group behind overturning Roe v
body:
[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/54940?refcode=em20261101-61951&t=1001&akid=61951%2E1407376%2EWIiTYf ]Demand Justice PAC[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/54940?refcode=em20261101-61951&t=1002&akid=61951%2E1407376%2EWIiTYf ]Demand Justice PAC

Ten federal
judges. One result: more power for corporations and the ultra-wealthy,
less for everyone else.

Together, they’re enabling the slide toward Oligarchy. Take a look:

#1: Judge Andrew Oldham: called our entire system of administrative law
“constitutionally suspect,” a view that threatens the EPA, OSHA, and the
CFPB.

#2: Chief Judge Reed O’Connor: ruled the entire Affordable Care Act
unconstitutional, a theory so extreme the Supreme Court reversed it 7-2.

#3: Chief Judge Amos Mazzant: struck down overtime pay for 4 million
workers and blocked a law targeting anonymous shell companies.

#4: Judge James C. Ho: reported 26 reimbursed trips, including a Cancun
junket paid for by the right-wing group behind overturning Roe v. Wade.

#5: Judge Don R. Willett: wants to revive the legal doctrine courts once
used to strike down minimum wage and child labor laws.

#6: Judge Edith H. Jones: argued for a theory that would have destroyed
the CFPB, the agency that has returned over $21 billion to consumers.

#7: Judge Victor Marrero: approved the T-Mobile/Sprint merger despite
objections from 14 state attorneys general. The combined company shed
roughly 14,000 jobs.

#8: Judge J. Campbell Barker: helped kill a rule that would have raised
franchise and contract workers’ pay by $1.06 billion a year.

#9: Judge Ada E. Brown: nullified the FTC’s non-compete ban, costing 30
million workers more than $400 billion in wages.

#10: Judge Sean D. Jordan: wiped out overtime protections for another 4
million workers, then killed a rule keeping medical debt off credit
reports.

Workers, consumers, and patients lose. Corporations and billionaires get
richer. Several of these judges have their lifestyles bankrolled by the
same conservative legal network shaping the bench, and we’re calling it
what it is: corruption.

Demand Justice PAC is fighting back: naming names, exposing the money and
influence behind these rulings, and fighting to restore independence to
our courts.

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55459?c0=dj-em-20261101.LiDVc0&refcode=em20261101-61951&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=61951%2E1407376%2EWIiTYf ]We can’t do it without grassroots supporters like you. Will you chip in
$5 today to help us fight the judges enabling the slide
toward Oligarchy?

name: Jen Kiggans
subject: Blossom
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Kiggans for Congress
body:
People often ask...how did I get that name?

People often ask...how did I get that name?
| [](https://trk.email.repdailyred.__NW2w)
---
That's a picture of me from when I flew H-46 and H-3 helicopters in the U.S. Navy. If you look to my left, you can see my call sign...**Blossom.**
People often ask...how did I get that name?
Well, my roommate in flight school and I went on a bit of a "girl power" kick one day and bought old bathtub non-skid flower stickers from the store, cut out that flower shape in reflective tape from our squadron, and stuck those reflective flowers on our helmets.
There is very little room for making a Navy flight suit more "feminine," but on cruise we were able to be a little more creative and came to love those girly flowers on our helmets.
Although the helicopter community doesn't use call signs as much as some of the fixed wing squadrons, the "Blossom" stuck and was painted on the side of a CH-46 for part of my first cruise. Made for a great photo and story!
It was my experience in the Navy that helped instill in me the importance of service.
Far too often, our elected officials today forget that their job is to SERVE. They think it is their job to tell everyone what to do and why everyone else is wrong....but that's not service.
As a Navy veteran and nurse practitioner, I got so frustrated and decided to run for Congress because I wanted to actually SERVE my country and my community.
**While for some it is all about power, for me it is all about service.**
Sadly, this has made me some enemies in Washington.
No one is going to buy me off or tell me what to do...I'm going to keep serving the people I represent, not serve some "master" in Washington, D.C.
If you are also tired of leaders who care more about power than service, [I'm asking you to send me some help today.](https://trk.email.repdailyred._)
Because I'm a veteran and not a career politician, I need all the help I can get to support my fight against the Democrats.
---
| [RUSH SUPPORT TO JEN](https://trk.email.repdailyred._-f8XwE6sXCUL9thkw)
---
I know this was a longer message than you are probably used to getting, but I want you to know where I'm coming from and why I need your help. Whether it's $100 or just $10, anything you can contribute will help this Navy veteran keep fighting back business as usual in D.C.
It's time we support leaders who truly want to serve our country, and that's what I promise to always do...are you with me, Peter?
With the courage to fight,
---
[](https://trk.email.repdailyred._-_ZyMv65e6Z2EMHqJQ9gQ)
---
-Jen
---

---
[](https://trk.email.repdailyred.)
---
I would not be where I am today without the help of my incredible and faithful supporters like you. Because of your support, I can keep fighting to make our country stronger.

Together we will get our country back on the right track and secure America's success!
---

## Fake Email Claims Hemp Rules Lifted
A fake email posing as a [Tennessee Alcoholic Beverage Commission (TABC)](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkb2O3DAQg5_G7mYhyX_rwkUad5c2pTGWxuvJ6ucgTSzk7QOnSJPyWhIk8JE_PrYPZM_x9R0DLSLHFqkWTyKUtwPfRAHZXxgd5Z29FLIpps0oM4LWoPSGVviircfWLbvRM_a2pUVPczd0ujPP9lysngxpsw9TNx6KkOzQIXXjU_eoTK9aXu5CrZXWWj376TGRnodxHKizxzyja3pFjiXlh5wkFCOVQnT43-mi_LAptH45RT5L031rzNqYtdb6qO8cb7Mx603VmPVfFP4T0Nt0Js8Wdroo44vAphC4FE4RPB9SIJMge_AcWAqkCHJaBEdeEGbA6OCdUVIAizHizgUOnyplCJj55y-MCJXINWZt8-I-K3vPZZyaXr3umf-CyBdfuBbzJwAA___ZWKF2) notice told licensed retailers Saturday morning that all restrictions on hemp products had been lifted. The message, [sent on what looked like official TABC letterhead](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJyk0L3uozAQBPCnMR2INTYfhYs0KE2idFeijb0OVoyNYA_u3v7EvcK_H82Mfr8e0wNDDOnzxIUMs58SnXskZtomj1-iBUM8MDna3iHyTjanPMlatiVAWcOElsNBk8LCmbeEAZUtyEA3NLqBRvbFbKzXtrWIRL5DRz36ptO9Hix5JOVsEcxVCFADQN2rruoIBt22mhrrhwGdUDW5wHmreCamlGjfiXz8mw_aKpuXIpqZed1FcxNyFHI8z7OyMzJjyvmD6QoJOV47Qo5QCzk2IOSopVadEnK8Y4z5JErla8P0LZ-5vMVY3mlZy9eW3W_LFe7rn2Izbj1DjGFvO6HqzwX0_wL_0O8w8l8AAAD__04JhKI), said stores could sell THCA, Delta-8, Delta-9, and other hemp products at any strength, claiming to undo the THCA ban that took effect July 1. It also cleared kratom for sale and made routine store inspections optional. Aaron Rummage, the commission’s policy and communications director, said the email came from an unidentified outside party. “ _Hemp restrictions remain in effect,”_ he said. In a follow-up notice to licensees, the commission said the fake email also claimed licensing accounts had been deleted, and it warned recipients not to click any links or reply. TABC’s laws, product limits, and inspection requirements all still stand.

Why I don't release a tape until it's bulletproof, and what's coming next.

| [ ](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckT-vnDAQxD-N6Th5d_lzFC4ina57aVOixV7AejZGxrxTvn3EJSnSptyZ2ZF-mh8f4wf74LflO0cxucxjPkZfUnBllejji4td_bb00GitR9TY1QC1hpFt8V8yNlw546xjsJUY6AdqCTukajXUO4d3BHbgoBfbNuxsO91xoOE-d_fKm6sPQAMAaYTb4ICGdhqYyDV9h6rRHCSXW5b9nIK3vBU-PueUrdxsilUwayn7oeibwqfC5yH2zHLjTVwqV0LhM32KzBLFeV5yOvdLikst4eCf4uq2jlO9p50VPc8SxyOd2Yqixz8hhd1lXi1nVPR4P_zWLMed_bIpevzBwb9O2opsRdEjl1lhxzGd75PaKhu3v3wI_uh61eglsg9vpPKfK3wZ_BUAAP__VKOWmg)

Dear Patriot, Right now, in campaign offices across this country, people are looking at the new volunteer a little differently, and [**that's exactly why I need you with me**](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckT-vnDAQxD-N6Th5d_lzFC4ina57aVOixV7AejZGxrxTvn3EJSnSptyZ2ZF-mh8f4wf74LflO0cxucxjPkZfUnBllejji4td_bb00GitR9TY1QC1hpFt8V8yNlw546xjsJUY6AdqCTukajXUO4d3BHbgoBfbNuxsO91xoOE-d_fKm6sPQAMAaYTb4ICGdhqYyDV9h6rRHCSXW5b9nIK3vBU-PueUrdxsilUwayn7oeibwqfC5yH2zHLjTVwqV0LhM32KzBLFeV5yOvdLikst4eCf4uq2jlO9p50VPc8SxyOd2Yqixz8hhd1lXi1nVPR4P_zWLMed_bIpevzBwb9O2opsRdEjl1lhxzGd75PaKhu3v3wI_uh61eglsg9vpPKfK3wZ_BUAAP__VKOWmg). Two weeks ago, I posted a warning to every midterm campaign in America: "We have undercover people inside midterm campaigns across the United States." And I told them: | "I'm watching every single thing you ALL are doing."
---
714,000 people saw that post. The campaigns saw it too. Then Detroit came out, and a man who swore he could spot one of us from across the room learned that he had been talking to one of my journalists all along.
So what's on the other tapes? **I can't tell you yet,** and I want you to understand exactly why, because the reason is the same thing that made Detroit hold up the moment it went public.
I said in that same post that we would not release footage until we had checked the facts, corroborated our sources and gotten comment, so that every story was **absolutely bulletproof.** That promise is the most expensive part of what we do. It means editors reviewing every hour of raw footage, researchers checking every claim against the public record, and calls to every person on tape to give them a chance to explain. Then the lawyers read every word. [**Help me keep that promise.**](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckT-vnDAQxD-N6Th5d_lzFC4ina57aVOixV7AejZGxrxTvn3EJSnSptyZ2ZF-mh8f4wf74LflO0cxucxjPkZfUnBllejji4td_bb00GitR9TY1QC1hpFt8V8yNlw546xjsJUY6AdqCTukajXUO4d3BHbgoBfbNuxsO91xoOE-d_fKm6sPQAMAaYTb4ICGdhqYyDV9h6rRHCSXW5b9nIK3vBU-PueUrdxsilUwayn7oeibwqfC5yH2zHLjTVwqV0LhM32KzBLFeV5yOvdLikst4eCf4uq2jlO9p50VPc8SxyOd2Yqixz8hhd1lXi1nVPR4P_zWLMed_bIpevzBwb9O2opsRdEjl1lhxzGd75PaKhu3v3wI_uh61eglsg9vpPKfK3wZ_BUAAP__VKOWmg)
[](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckT-vnDAQxD-N6Th5d_lzFC4ina57aVOixV7AejZGxrxTvn3EJSnSptyZ2ZF-mh8f4wf74LflO0cxucxjPkZfUnBllejji4td_bb00GitR9TY1QC1hpFt8V8yNlw546xjsJUY6AdqCTukajXUO4d3BHbgoBfbNuxsO91xoOE-d_fKm6sPQAMAaYTb4ICGdhqYyDV9h6rRHCSXW5b9nIK3vBU-PueUrdxsilUwayn7oeibwqfC5yH2zHLjTVwqV0LhM32KzBLFeV5yOvdLikst4eCf4uq2jlO9p50VPc8SxyOd2Yqixz8hhd1lXi1nVPR4P_zWLMed_bIpevzBwb9O2opsRdEjl1lhxzGd75PaKhu3v3wI_uh61eglsg9vpPKfK3wZ_BUAAP__VKOWmg)
It also means I won't rush. If a story is ready before Tuesday, you'll see it. If it needs one more source, it waits. I would rather be right than first, because when the denials come, and they always come, our story has to be the one still standing. Detroit showed what happens when we do it right: a campaign statement, a party statement and a staffer who is no longer employed. The next one will be held to the same standard. [**Help me get it out the door.**](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckT-vnDAQxD-N6Th5d_lzFC4ina57aVOixV7AejZGxrxTvn3EJSnSptyZ2ZF-mh8f4wf74LflO0cxucxjPkZfUnBllejji4td_bb00GitR9TY1QC1hpFt8V8yNlw546xjsJUY6AdqCTukajXUO4d3BHbgoBfbNuxsO91xoOE-d_fKm6sPQAMAaYTb4ICGdhqYyDV9h6rRHCSXW5b9nIK3vBU-PueUrdxsilUwayn7oeibwqfC5yH2zHLjTVwqV0LhM32KzBLFeV5yOvdLikst4eCf4uq2jlO9p50VPc8SxyOd2Yqixz8hhd1lXi1nVPR4P_zWLMed_bIpevzBwb9O2opsRdEjl1lhxzGd75PaKhu3v3wI_uh61eglsg9vpPKfK3wZ_BUAAP__VKOWmg) Covering the $47,000 we spent on Detroit is what lets my team stay focused on the next release instead of the last bill. **We have two days left.**

clean_body: Why I don't release a tape until it's bulletproof, and what's coming next. | Dear Patriot, Right now, in campaign offices across this country, people are looking at the new volunteer a little differently, and . Two weeks ago, I posted a warning to every midterm campaign in America: "We have undercover people inside midterm campaigns across the United States." And I told them: | "I'm watching every single thing you ALL are doing." 714,000 people saw that post. The campaigns saw it too. Then Detroit came out, and a man who swore he could spot one of us from across the room learned that he had been talking to one of my journalists all along. So what's on the other tapes? I can't tell you yet, and I want you to understand exactly why, because the reason is the same thing that made Detroit hold up the moment it went public. I said in that same post that we would not release footage until we had checked the facts, corroborated our sources and gotten comment, so that every story was absolutely bulletproof. That promise is the most expensive part of what we do. It means editors reviewing every hour of raw footage, researchers checking every claim against the public record, and calls to every person on tape to give them a chance to explain. Then the lawyers read every word. It also means I won't rush. If a story is ready before Tuesday, you'll see it. If it needs one more source, it waits. I would rather be right than first, because when the denials come, and they always come, our story has to be the one still standing. Detroit showed what happens when we do it right: a campaign statement, a party statement and a staffer who is no longer employed. The next one will be held to the same standard. Covering the $47,000 we spent on Detroit is what lets my team stay focused on the next release instead of the last bill. We have two days left. You and your family deserve to know what's said behind these doors before you vote, and long after. | | | | | | Thank you for everything you do. In Truth, James O'Keefe Founder, O'Keefe Media Group P.S. Every campaign in America knows we're out there. Not one of them knows where. | Pop Acta Media | Republican Task Force PO Box 461 Fort Collins, CO 80522 | _

## U.S. Approves Missile Sales to Ukraine
The State Department on Friday [approved a $2.1 billion sale](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAQRL8GMiPaZgwEDi6ZbC69EDWmPeMbY1t2L2j_fsVq_2CzVpdeqar-PZYH-uDj8y_uZNilJdJZAzFTWXLKvr59fFayhbgmt2OpGLdF9lILANHDgpb9QQu0m3FEklRLBsZZ3ZQcQbcv4wjxNkpSesN5moHsoCdataNxpqEfWm8uO4AeABTcVKenyaEaaSVtx1W5Zuhp85xK9z_5yC9y4TMdVDqb9jaYF3OujfrTyHsj7-d5dnG1V41Lvz6phK2R9493QR_puqrAnEs6qAoJYvUh-BRFxUAiIxefWPjIVCxlTqWKH1QUG1H3Wg_QFrPl8wKrHpuhf-7ow3cg_t2Mh5FfAQAA__8u14o6) of 500 Patriot interceptor missiles to Ukraine, a deal involving no U.S. funds. The department named Lockheed Martin the principal contractor and said the sale would have "no adverse impact" on U.S. defense readiness. Kyiv will [cover the cost with donations](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLsO3CAURL8Gd1g8_NqCIo27TZvSwnBZ3xiDxWXX2nx95PxCupFGmtE5v57L02LE9PppDzA15CXBRRFqhbKc-UTaMb0IXIFKORy2kE1-UUINXEou5GJdxQ8ssvEmACjQDRg5PnSv1SiHZjMP0YmpF8pK1_XuMblOKLV65X2wYwiyQXPPSSmklFr2uh2mKVg9wgqDG1cdWCfAY82l_Z0x1Q1C_OYPlNblo4lmq_Ukpn8wNTM1X9fVupVujLtnar4jU_N7LxYT8NPWgrnyA4kwAvE38ZjdvgF4fthSMXGyEfgfiJBo_36Zmpti_HlhjEjDyDrxOizGf__1_6x9jPobAAD__w0xhJw) from Canada, Germany, and Norway. The sale follows warnings from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky that his country had [nearly run out](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkc2OnDAQhJ_G3HqEbf7mwGGiiNvmmByRwW1w1rgtuwe0bx-RV9hzSVX66vvzMX8YH3zcfpkDR3Y0R7xKQGbMc6Lky6ePW8E1Ixdyh8nFRDurWnUgJdRyNiv7E2dZ2dEhKtQVjrJ_6larXnbVPrbGdcPwXCQOdml0uzjTNrZVepDN0j5t5ce7TspaSqllqx_dMDije1ywW_tFO9HUaD1TfvwlH3lHF77oxPxY6ajCuDOnIvRLqEmo6bqux1HinQk1YYRtEWq6qYSaiHfMQk3vAialTCcWMJAyJSpoQUlYfAieIhQTEMhBMpw9MfjImFdMTLkAE7w_s_ERwTjGDCYE3NDCTsG-k1CTyfB6qS1_NZvQE63eCv3zx_0zXuU35lTl0abrHitdL5p6O4wP_4H4exrOUf0LAAD__5DCoFE) of the interceptors it relies on to stop Russian ballistic missiles, as tensions with the Trump administration escalated.

**Whatever happened to Jiffy Pop?** For about two decades, the surest sign that something good was about to happen in an American kitchen was the sound of popping coming from a foil-covered pan being shaken on a burner. Jiffy Pop was a snack, a science experiment, and a babysitter all at once, until the microwave quietly put it out of work. It started in LaPorte, Indiana, where chemist Frederick Mennen took an earlier foil-pan product called E-Z Pop, gave it a sturdier handle and a better dome, and began marketing it as Jiffy Pop in 1959. By 1961, one California plant was turning out 15,000 pans a day. [You can see one of the early TV ads here.](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuqzAUxvGnMVuQj01sGDxcKTdbulXthszhENwaTPEJNG9f0Vfo-n3Sb_i_3dqbDzHM9xc_keMhtTPtORIzre2SlpA_w3zPhCtxTsPk1-znvlVSmRPASULrkcNGLRS9G4gU6YIc2EaftbJgitFZX3mQEk2Nte0RmkraCi36RhrEThfBHRyABAANZ12auh68ttSRQdvpQVSS-sBpLT9SmHmkIT7TRmuJaSqiG5mXLPQ_oa5CXfd9L5_pwY-Ojv9YPOMo9HUT-vK-N1X3hZfX7__F6vplDzGGbKyo5H3yIf6S_LcQm1M_AQAA__98YnJ2) The jingle promised it was "as much fun to make as it is to eat," which was true, and also a dare. You held the wire handle, moved the pan in slow circles, watched the foil [swell into a silver balloon](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFu6yAUgOGnwVssDsTGHhjulepO6dCl3RA2h5gWGwtOgvL2VfoKnX_pG_6Pi7nYEMN-fbMbavLJ7FhLRCLM5khHKN9hvxZcMlJJfrO52N0ZwUV_AjhxMHahcEcDjdMeUaBsUIMaZSeFgr5ZtZPeq3FcFHfziELKcUDoQPBudBKGuQn6yQFwAJDQybYfBm-lwhn7Rc3SszNHFyjl9iuFnVb08ZHumNslbU3UK9FRmPzHxMTEVGttH-lGtxmfnYmprClTYWI67dPy_vny37zWJmt31BBjKL1iZ37dbIi_Hv3twl2LnwAAAP__FH1xcQ) the size of a basketball, and listened for the moment the popping slowed. Somebody always scorched it. Somebody always ate it anyway. The end came from just a few feet away on the countertop. Orville Redenbacher rolled out shelf-stable microwave popcorn in 1983, and the category exploded from $53 million in sales that year to $250 million by 1987. Three minutes and no shaking beat five minutes and a hot handle. Jiffy Pop never actually died, though. Conagra still owns it, still makes it in [one flavor, butter](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOoCAYhJ8GO4w_KGhBcY3dXnulQfhR9hAIsJp9-4v3Ctt-k0xmvj8f24f2wcfjt75QNZe2iE8N2BqWLafs618fj4qmYKvJXbpUHe3GBiYoAB1g06b5GzforHKIDHmHCuTCJ84kiO5UYlqWcZ9AmEWO0nLuJinsPEmzjyj2ufPqrQMYAIDDxHsxz05ziTsKI3fuyDig9S2V_jP52E504TvdWHqTri6os7VcCf9F2ErY-jxPf-L-ZoStuST7ZRq12LQPhK2f3rlvmlOm-9d7krqg71TQvsykEmlt6caW8guyjwfNOhK2wsSBia4omx8fgq9CknE4Lu3D_x3tZ_Zuxf4FAAD__1-Yhf4), and still sells it for about $2.50 a pan, usually on the bottom shelf near the microwave bags. Campers swear by it. So do fans of the 1996 opening scene in _Scream_ , where a pan burning on the stove became one of horror's great nervous-stomach props. It lost the convenience war decades ago. It is still, pop for pop, one of the best shows in the kitchen. _Did you pop Jiffy Pop back in the day? Let us know your thoughts by replying to this email._

For about two decades, the surest sign that something good was about to happen in an American kitchen was the sound of popping coming from a foil-covered pan being shaken on a burner. Jiffy Pop was a snack, a science experiment, and a babysitter all at once, until the microwave quietly put it out of work. It started in LaPorte, Indiana, where chemist Frederick Mennen took an earlier foil-pan product called E-Z Pop, gave it a sturdier handle and a better dome, and began marketing it as Jiffy Pop in 1959. By 1961, one California plant was turning out 15,000 pans a day. The jingle promised it was "as much fun to make as it is to eat," which was true, and also a dare. You held the wire handle, moved the pan in slow circles, watched the foil the size of a basketball, and listened for the moment the popping slowed. Somebody always scorched it. Somebody always ate it anyway. The end came from just a few feet away on the countertop. Orville Redenbacher rolled out shelf-stable microwave popcorn in 1983, and the category exploded from $53 million in sales that year to $250 million by 1987. Three minutes and no shaking beat five minutes and a hot handle. Jiffy Pop never actually died, though. Conagra still owns it, still makes it in , and still sells it for about $2.50 a pan, usually on the bottom shelf near the microwave bags. Campers swear by it. So do fans of the 1996 opening scene in Scream , where a pan burning on the stove became one of horror's great nervous-stomach props. It lost the convenience war decades ago. It is still, pop for pop, one of the best shows in the kitchen. Did you pop Jiffy Pop back in the day? Today is the final day of early voting in Ohio. Already, we've broken records for the number of ballots cast before Election Day. As of last night, 1,595,206 Ohioans have already voted. Because of you, we're making history.
We're closing in on our opportunity to turn the page on Jon Husted's failures and send a loud message that Ohioans should come before billionaires and special interests.
Every day, this campaign proves that we have more power together than those greedy billionaires ever will. I'm honored to play a role in sending that message.
This race will be a nail-biter - that's a fact. But I know that we can win. With just one more push.
**We 're getting our closing message out to Ohioans all over this state. [I can't do it without you. I'm asking you to pitch in to fund our final campaign push. Please donate now, if you can.](https://substack.com/redirect/bc4d2675-483b-4970-9f19-98f60998c97e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
I know we can win because Ohioans can see more money going out than coming in, and they're tired of it.
Because they heard Donald Trump and Jon Husted promise to lower their costs over and over, just to turn around and give tax breaks to the ultra-wealthy, _not_ Ohio families.
Because folks in all 88 counties are fed up with this corrupt system, and we're fighting back.
Early voting in Ohio will wrap up in just a few hours.
We're watching early voting data live. We can see which counties are overperforming and if there are any areas that aren't keeping pace. We can see where there are voters who should turn out in support for our campaign and ensure we can get organizers and volunteers in their communities to mobilize them in time.
Every dollar we raise right now goes toward reaching those voters before polls close, and will make sure we have the staff capacity to hold the line on Election Day too.
So now, I have one question for you.
_Are you ready to win this election together?_
We can do this, but we have to give everything we can. I need you with me more than ever. If you have the means,**[I'd like to ask if you can contribute to my campaign to help us run through the tape](https://substack.com/redirect/bc4d2675-483b-4970-9f19-98f60998c97e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[.](https://substack.com/redirect/bc4d2675-483b-4970-9f19-98f60998c97e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) If you can't, it'd mean a lot if you can forward this to someone who can.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/bc4d2675-483b-4970-9f19-98f60998c97e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=5574704&post_id=222962681&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjIyOTYyNjgxLCJpYXQiOjE3OTM1MzcwNzksImV4cCI6MTc5NjEyOTA3OSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTU1NzQ3MDQiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.x3Xi4INh0IGB9SceOHBeNr18ncFSfqWUdvXVv6g53uQ)
Thank you for meeting this moment with energy, enthusiasm, and action. I'm beyond grateful.
Sherrod Brown

**[If you have the means, please consider pledging to support Sherrod Brown's campaign today. Everything will add up and put us one step closer to flipping the Senate in November.](https://substack.com/redirect/bc4d2675-483b-4970-9f19-98f60998c97e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

[ stdin# ]Josh Shapiro for Pennsylvania
We’ve truly reached an unprecedented moment here in Pennsylvania.

Across the Commonwealth, our opponent is running AI-generated attack ads
against our campaign — spending HUGE SUMS of cash to blast out deepfake
videos of Josh Shapiro to mislead voters and change the outcome of this
entire election.

Derek, we’ve seen
the data ourselves: When our opponent’s attack ads go without a proper
response, we lose our momentum. Simple as that. [ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/22742?t=1001&akid=901%2E245147%2EBVHO-j ]So please, with just
TWO days left to reach thousands of undecided voters across Pennsylvania,
will you rush $5 or more right now to make sure our opponent’s AI attacks
can’t hand this election — and our entire democracy — over to Donald
Trump?

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/22742?t=1002&akid=901%2E245147%2EBVHO-j ]Rush $5 →

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/22743?t=1003&akid=901%2E245147%2EBVHO-j ]Other →

Derek, we haven’t
seen an election like this.

Negative ads, misleading smears — we’re used to those. Sure, they can do
serious damage when left without a response. But with a proper strategy in
place (and a generous team of supporters!), we know how to fight back.

But now that AI has entered our elections? The rulebook has been thrown
out the window.

Derek, we don’t

but we know it’s a lot. And the ONLY way we’ll feel confident about
Election Day is if we reach as many voters as possible — in-person —
before Tuesday morning.

name: Abdul
subject: What I'm thinking about over coffee this morning
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Abdul for U
body:
Peter, I've got my morning espresso in hand, and some thoughts to share with you.
It’s November 1st, and Election Day is this Tuesday. It feels _crazy_ to type that out, but here we are.
I can't stop thinking about how we got here.
Last year in April, I remember talking to 5 people in a room. At the start of this campaign, we hosted events in small coffee shops, and our entire staff fit in one car.
Now, we have an army of 25,000 volunteers; we’ve brought this campaign to hundreds of cities and packed venues with thousands of supporters, and we’ve broken fundraising records with this incredible grassroots team.
_**You**_**did that, Peter.** You chipped in when it was hard, you showed up, you spread the word, and you've stood by my side day in and day out.
Now, it all comes down to the next couple of days.
Tons of Michiganders still don't know who they're voting for. A lot of them don't even know there's an election on Tuesday.
And let me be clear — that's not a knock on them. People are busy working two jobs, getting the kids to school, trying to afford groceries. It shouldn't be this hard to keep up, and politics is the last thing on their mind.
**But these folks may hold the fate of this election in their hands.** The last time Mike Rogers ran for this seat, it came down to 20,217 votes. If it’s that close again, it’ll truly come down to these last-minute voters.
MAGA Republicans are spending $157 million to try and bring those folks onto their side. We can’t outspend that, so our job is simple. Find every one of these undecided voters and make sure they:
A. Have a plan to vote, and know where and when.
B. Hear from _us,_ so they'll vote in support of a campaign that's fighting for working people.
That means organizers on the doors, volunteers on the phones, and our message on every screen we can reach. All of it costs money. I've never taken a dime from corporate PACs, so I'm not asking them. I'm asking you, Peter.
**Will you chip in $5 or whatever you can afford to help us reach every Michigander who still needs a plan to vote before Tuesday?**
[**https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-ms-aes-20261101-1-ak**](https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20261101-1-ak.0ecxdv&amount=5&refcode=em20261101-3825&t=2&akid=3848%2E251025%2EWPiSVf)
Thank you for supporting our campaign in the final stretch.
Your friend in the fight,
Abdul

WIN more races. ** It's what Charlie called "the clipboard and tennis shoes" work to reach every voter. Last week a polling firm asked Americans about a tech CEO named Marshall Ancoates. He does not exist. He was invented by PF Global as a control. Twenty-two percent of the country pegged him as a Republican anyway, against 18 percent who guessed Democrat -- and Trump 2024 voters went 30-to-19 for the Republican. Harris voters split evenly, at 24.
Sit with that. A fictional executive acquired a party affiliation from thin air, and the affiliation everyone reached for was red. The electorate is no longer reading tech executives. It is reading a category, and the category has been painted.
The paint is mostly one man's. Elon Musk is read Republican by 59 percent of Americans -- and unlike everyone else on the list, he earned it, putting at least $276 million into Republican causes in a single quarter, by far the largest spender of the cycle. That is a real fact. It is also a fact about one man, and it has bleached across an entire industry that does not share his ledger.

Patriot,

Most of what we send you is strategy: states, numbers, the plan to win. This one is about why we do this work at all. And that starts with Charlie Kirk.

Charlie launched Turning Point in the shadows of the Obama re-election campaign headquarters in Chicago. He was 18 years old.

Every established political force on the Left and the Right tried to stop him.

They failed.

What Charlie started grew into what is **the most influential activist organization in modern American history**.

We were privileged to work with him and be a part of this movement.

We joined Charlie because we believed our mission was the only viable way to save this country. Charlie was willing to do what nobody else in the conservative movement would do. He went looking for young Americans who cared enough about this country to act, and he gave them a reason to fight.

Then came 2020...

Under President Biden, we saw corruption, weaponization of the government, and a government promoting values that put Americans last.

Charlie was adamant that we do everything we could possibly do to fix this in 2024. **We DID IT** , and we must continue for 2026 and 2028 to have a shot at saving this country.

Now, it is on us to continue Charlie's vision and mission.

Every single day, we work to continue his legacy of recruiting, training, and mobilizing a new generation of citizens who love this country enough to do something about it.

That work does not stop at the campus gates. It's now changing the direction of the nation.

Right now, ballot chasers supported by Turning Point PAC are in the field in **states that will determine not just 2026, but the 2028 Presidential election**.

They are meeting voters face to face. They are building real relationships in these communities. They are chasing every ballot, whether it's cast on Election Day or by mail.

This is how we build the Red Wall.

Election Day is November 3rd.

clean_body: This election depends on the work we do now. Can you help us get to the finish line? | | | Friend, I know the partisan noise is getting louder. I know that your inbox, TV, and social media are all being flooded with political content. But with only two days until Election Day, there is only one thing that actually matters — and that’s voter turnout. Right now, we’re laser-focused on making sure every voter has a plan to vote by Election Day. = The stakes for our families couldn’t be higher. With a Democratic majority in Congress, we can finally get back to work fighting to lower costs, protecting reproductive rights, expanding access to health care, and preserving our Bay. When I think about this Tuesday, I am thinking about the opportunity to make real change and take meaningful steps to solve the challenges facing our neighbors. This work is never about making headlines or winning partisan fights online. It is about showing up, doing the work, and connecting with every single person we can before the polls close. = | = I can’t guarantee an outcome, but I can guarantee my full effort. We are working around the clock to support our state and local partners — and send a blue wave to Congress. Thank you for standing with us, Sarah Elfreth | * | | | ---|---|---|--- Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth broke barriers in 2024, becoming the youngest woman ever elected to Congress from Maryland. She went to Congress with one thing in mind: delivering for Maryland families on the issues that matter most. Whether it's standing up for federal workers, supporting veterans, protecting the Chesapeake Bay, or tackling the affordability crisis head-on, Sarah is on the front lines, fighting for what is right. And Sarah has delivered on her promises. She has spent her first year in the House advocating for the Third District, successfully passing five bills into law, solving over 1,000 constituent cases, and bringing tens of millions in funding back to her community. She learned her work ethic and tenacity from growing up in a union household and honed her skills of problem-solving and collaborating over six years in the Maryland State Senate. name: Mark Kelly
subject: My decision:
body:
Hey folks,
it’s Mark Kelly.

Seven years ago, I was making a decision about whether I was going to run
for the Senate.

I knew it would be a lot of work. A lot of time away from home. A lot of
time away from family. I knew it wouldn’t be easy.

But after two years of Donald Trump and a Republican-held Senate doing
just about everything he wanted, I knew I couldn’t sit on the sidelines. I
had to do something.

So, I ran. And, somehow, we won. And then we had to turn around and run
all over again to win a full term after that. But thanks to your support,
we won that one, too.

I’m grateful every day that I get to wake up, walk out the door, and
defend our people, our democracy, and our Constitution. It’s one of the
greatest honors of my life. And I’ve never forgotten that I wouldn’t be
here without your help.

I know we’ve been in some tough fights before, but this one is different.
With elections coming this November, the stakes are higher than they have
ever been. The fate of our democracy hangs in the balance.

After everything that’s already happened, I wish I didn’t have to ask you
for more. But that’s what I need to do.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261101_2.lH9fIm&refcode=em20261101-2&t=1001&akid=9883%2E582294%2Es7rpDX ]I’m asking you to split a donation between Chris Pappas and me. We’re
going to do everything we can to take back Congress this November, and
Chris Pappas needs your help. I just hope you know that I wouldn’t be
asking if this wasn’t important.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261101_2.lH9fIm&amount=5&refcode=em20261101-2&t=1020&akid=9883%2E582294%2Es7rpDX ]Donate $5 »

Thank you.

Mark

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261101_2.lH9fIm&refcode=em20261101-2&t=1021&akid=9883%2E582294%2Es7rpDX ][IMG]

You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:
http://act.chrispappas.org/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?akid=9883%2E582294%2Es7rpDX

In a battleground district like mine, one point is barely a lead. We need to work around the clock the next two days to widen the gap and win.
2. **Donald Trump’s shady super PAC is spending more in MI-04 than almost any other district.** The National GOP knows this race is tight, and they’re spending whatever they think it takes to win.
3. **With just 2 days until Election Day our fundraising has slowed down.** We saw a surge in donations ahead of our final end-of-month fundraising deadline (thank you!), but since then our numbers have dipped. We can’t afford to slow down.

**No one here is panicking. We don’t have much time to turn things around — but we know we can with your help. If we’re going to defeat Huizenga and flip this seat, we need to step up our fundraising. I want to be clear about this — I’m not in this race to “come close” or “make Huizenga sweat,” or “give Republicans a real scare.” I’m in this race to win it. Hi there, it's Michele Tafoya!

If I were to take a guess, there's a 50/50 chance you may recognize me from a stadium's big screen.
If that's not the case, I get it... Let me at least tell you briefly about who I am and what I'm about anyway!

I should clarify first, no, I didn't make my career running for touchdowns or kicking game-winning field goals.

I worked as a sideline reporter in professional football for nearly three decades. Working in the sport for that long was a dream come true, and I wouldn't have wanted it any other way.

clean_body: Many of our women’s races could come down to a few hundred votes. | = It’s November 1, Peter, and you know what that means: After months of recruitment, strategizing, and organizing, the final countdown to Election Day is here. But our work isn’t finished yet. My team and I are keeping a close eye on each and every one of our candidates’ races, and let me be clear: The data show that from statehouses to governorships to Congress, EMILYs List women are competing in races that could come down to just a few hundred votes. So with less than 48 hours left until Election Day, now is not the time to sit back and hope for the best. This is the moment when your support will be put immediately to work turning out every last voter and delivering decisive victories for our women up and down the ballot. = | = Over the past several months, we’ve watched momentum build behind our women in races all across the country — and MAGA Republicans are seeing it, too. That’s why they’re ready to do — and spend — whatever it takes to cling to power. They’re already calling in megadonors to flood the airwaves and spread last-minute misinformation about our candidates in these final days. And we need to be prepared for them to try and dispute results they don’t like after the election, too. This is not the time for complacency, Peter. A child's ZIP code should tell us where they live. It should not tell us how little we expect them to achieve.
Yet too often, when children struggle to read, the explanations arrive faster than the solutions. Poverty. Family circumstances. Funding. Another study. Another committee. Racism?
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2768453d-e857-4d20-b8ea-9a63f5759e1d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Meanwhile, childhood does not pause.
▶️ **[Watch the forum here.](https://substack.com/redirect/2768453d-e857-4d20-b8ea-9a63f5759e1d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
We brought together educators, policy experts, pastors, parents, and community voices because improving education requires people willing to work across those lines.
Parents need answers they can act on. Educators need approaches that help children learn. And communities need to insist that children's potential matters more than adults' attachment to the way things have always been done.
**We cannot prepare children for the opportunities of tomorrow while accepting that they cannot read today.**
Artificial intelligence is accelerating. Work is changing. New opportunities are emerging. Our children deserve the preparation to take their share of that future.
Literacy is where that preparation begins.
**Watch the conversation. Then share it with a parent, teacher, pastor, school board member, or neighbor.** Ask them: What should we put into practice--and how can we help?
**[Watch"Can Philadelphia Become the Next Mississippi Miracle?"](https://substack.com/redirect/2768453d-e857-4d20-b8ea-9a63f5759e1d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
And leave a comment: **What is one change you believe would make the greatest difference for Philadelphia 's children?**
Thank you to everyone who participated, attended, and supported this forum. Let's keep the conversation moving toward action.
Blessings...
Let's get to work!

As we approach Election Day, I've been thinking a lot about what this campaign has meant to me. Over the past several months, I've met people from every corner of our district. Republicans, Democrats, independents, and, frankly, plenty of folks who are simply tired of politics altogether.And one thing has become very clear: **People are fed up with these Trump sycophants who are squarely focused on selling you out and lining their own pockets.**_Same here. _ You know what we _do_ want? We want good jobs, affordable health care, safe neighborhoods, strong schools, and a better future for our children.These aren't red or blue issues. They're American issues. I didn't get into this race because I wanted to spend my time fighting with my neighbors. I got into it because I believe we can accomplish a whole lot more when we start listening to one another.**We don't have to agree on everything to work together on the things that matter. ** That's the kind of leadership I believe in. A government that listens more than it lectures. That brings more people to the table instead of shutting them out. I'm incredibly proud of what we've built together during this campaign. And I'm grateful to every person who has shared their story, volunteered their time, donated, or put their faith in what we're trying to accomplish. **We have far more in common than the politicians in Washington would have us believe. Because at the end of the day, we're neighbors first. And we're all in this together. ** **[So if you can, please consider donating to our campaign to flip TX-2, reject extremism, and to finally bring decency and integrity back to Washington.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142657303/657633267/-457524515?refcode=em1101&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTkyNDYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZDVjNGI3YTgtZmRkNS1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNTQ0NDJlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=1lT6zmJby4lAS_-6hQoG904u4BUkVbB9Trq-tXvHl1s=)**

body:
# [](https://act.janepac.com/go/30?t=1&akid=14%2E6803%2EMHFETL)
As we approach the final two days before Election Day, I want to start off by saying **thank you.**
Because of you, we’ve built an unstoppable movement of climate fighters—one that will outlast whatever happens on Tuesday. Whether you chipped in five bucks, signed petitions to protect our public lands, knocked doors, or talked to neighbors about what's at stake, you showed up when it mattered most.
Thank you again.
Come Tuesday, we have a real shot at celebrating historic wins in the most consequential races for our climate and our democracy. Here’s what I’m watching closely as final votes are cast:
**In Pennsylvania:** Mark Pinsley, Eileen Hartnett Albillar, Chris Thomas, and Brian Wrightson are in tight battles to flip red State Senate districts and secure a Democratic majority for the first time in over 30 years.
**In Wisconsin:** Robyn Vining, Trevor Jung, and Jenna Jacobson are taking on massive waves of dark money to flip state legislative seats and put power back in the hands of the people.
**In Georgia and Florida:** Peter Hubbard and Shelia Edwards are running for the Public Service Commission to hold utility monopolies accountable, while in Florida, Jennifer Jenkins and Angie Nixon are putting seats on the map for Congress and the U.S. Senate that were once written off.
**In Texas:** Clayton Tucker and Gina Hinojosa are going toe-to-toe with fossil fuel giants in the very heart of oil and gas country. Gina could unseat oil-money-lover Greg Abbott in the Texas governor’s race.
**In California and Michigan:** Randy Villegas and Will Lawrence are in two of the most competitive congressional races this year. They’ve made their entire campaigns about putting working people over the corporations who’ve sold us out.
This is a winner-takes-all moment. There is no second place. Big Oil, Elon Musk, and Trump-aligned super PACs are dumping everything they have into buying these seats at the eleventh hour. But our candidates don't rely on them — **they rely on you.**
**[We’ve come too far to slow down now. The next 48 hours are our final chance to make a difference. Will you please rush a $5 donation before polls close?](https://act.janepac.com/go/9?c0=ms_jfcp_em_20261101-ak.f1aVBD&amount=5&refcode=em20261101-14&t=3&akid=14%2E6803%2EMHFETL)**

Thank you for refusing to back down.
In solidarity,
xx Jane

Peter, it’s Governor Wes Moore. I will work with anybody. **_But I will bow to nobody_**. I didn’t come from money or prestige. As the son of an immigrant single mother, I came from hard work, community, and an unshakeable belief that _we could do better_. [If you share that belief, would you split a donation of $10 between our re-election campaign and the Democratic Party of Georgia today?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142666914/657651601/1183156290?amount=10&source=DPG_EM_FR_110126_B1_MooreSplit_S2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTA4MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3NDEwZmMwMi0wMWQ2LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=C_5fxuidBTCkQkgxGiIjTtQ6xToWvS9ifXdVQBg-sqA=) Peter, my grandfather was run out of his home by the Klan. **But he rebuilt anyway.** That history and resilience is why I believe every family deserves a fair shot at work, wages, and wealth — not just survival. clean_body: If you’d like to unsubscribe, | | = Peter, it’s Governor Wes Moore. I will work with anybody. But I will bow to nobody. I didn’t come from money or prestige. As the son of an immigrant single mother, I came from hard work, community, and an unshakeable belief that we could do better. = Peter, my grandfather was run out of his home by the Klan. But he rebuilt anyway. That history and resilience is why I believe every family deserves a fair shot at work, wages, and wealth — not just survival. Wednesday morning, early, state investigators came for the mayor of Kissimmee. By midday there was a booking photo -- glasses, neutral expression, the genre's uniform. By two o'clock, Florida's attorney general stood at a podium in Orlando beside the state's chief financial officer and the FDLE commissioner to announce that Mayor Jackie Espinosa, fifty-eight, the first Hispanic woman to hold the office by local accounts, was charged with one count of grand theft -- $20,000 to $100,000, a second-degree felony carrying up to fifteen years -- and one count of organized scheme to defraud. Her lawyer says she maintains her innocence, and that is where the law properly begins: an arrest is an allegation wearing handcuffs.
But the warrant tells a larger story than one mayor. It tells you how political crime gets cleaned up in 2026 -- not at the ballot box, but before it.

Friends,
With early voting underway in Kansas and Election Day just days away, Roger Marshall is _panicking_. After all, Roll Call named him one of the most vulnerable senators in the country and _multiple_ election experts have switched this race from a safe seat to a toss-up.
And you know what? He should be anxious. After turning his back on Kansans and consistently voting to make their lives harder and more expensive, people are fed up. They’re ready for a leader who will listen to them and work to solve their problems, not be a yes-man to a party and an administration that doesn’t put hardworking Kansas families first.
But Sen. Marshall has what he’s hoping is an ace up his sleeve: **President Trump is returning to Kansas today to hold another rally supporting Marshall.**
The president coming here again so close to Election Day is proof that Washington insiders are worried. _They know people are fed up, they know our grassroots movement is surging and they know we have what it takes to win._
**But folks, I’m worried too.** When the president rallies for someone, big money often follows. Top GOP super PACs have already spent nearly $40 million on this race, and after today, they’re almost certainly going to pour even more resources into defeating us.
**They’re pulling out all the stops because they know that, unlike me, Roger Marshall is a yes-man for party bosses. He’s spent a decade in Washington rubber-stamping the policies his party has told him to support, even when those policies hurt the people he was elected to represent.**
In the past year alone, he’s voted to slash the healthcare assistance that thousands of Kansans rely on, supported Medicaid cuts that have put 28 rural hospitals at risk of closing, backed a war that’s driven diesel prices to record highs and signed off on the tariffs that cost Kansans hundreds of dollars every month.
**Now, the establishment is going all out to save this seat for him so he can keep putting Washington insiders over Kansans.**
Look, the reality is that we have what it takes to retire Roger Marshall. If we didn’t, the president wouldn’t be coming back to try and rescue him. But that doesn’t change the fact that Marshall and his allies continue to outspend us at an alarming rate. They’re blanketing the airwaves with attack ads against me — and if we can’t find a way to keep up, we may lose the chance to defeat Marshall and flip this seat.
I know Kansans are ready for change. I know their enthusiasm for better leadership — leadership that actually fights for _them_ — is surging. But if we can’t keep ads on the air and fund our get-out-the-vote efforts, we’ll lose ground in this critical moment ... and we won’t have time to make it up.
**My team and I have set a rapid-response goal to raise $250,000 to help us meet this moment. That’s what it will take to respond to the escalated attacks that are coming. Peter, With just 2 days left before Election Day, we’re in the most important stretch of our campaign. Right now, our amazing team of supporters and volunteers are talking with voters all across NY-16 during these final days of GOTV. They’re knocking on doors, making phone calls, and meeting New Yorkers where they are – because every conversation in this final stretch makes all the difference. In these final hours, we have to mobilize our base and persuade every remaining undecided voter. This election will decide our country’s future, so we refuse to leave anything to chance. Once the polls close on November 3rd, we won’t get a second chance. If we want to see a Democratic House majority, it starts by protecting this seat. After nearly two years representing this district in Congress it's hard to believe we're already this close to another Election Day.
I've been thinking a lot about what these past two years have meant to me.
When voters elected me in 2024, they gave me the responsibility of representing their families, their communities and their concerns in Washington.

Hi, it's Chris.
**We have less than 48 hours left in this campaign, and New Hampshire is on the line.**
John Sununu has taken the lead in the polls, thanks to over $67 million in GOP spending that's flooding the airwaves.
We're running out of time to close this fundraising gap and keep the Granite State blue.
**[Will you chip in $15 or whatever you can afford to boost our grassroots campaign in its final days and help us flip the Senate?](https://substack.com/redirect/a605042c-bece-4b3d-99df-2486342203c3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ DONATE](https://substack.com/redirect/a605042c-bece-4b3d-99df-2486342203c3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**When I first ran for Congress, I made the decision that I wouldn 't take a dime of corporate PAC money.**
Not because I thought it would make campaigns easier. And not because I believed everyone else had to make the same decision.
I made that commitment because I wanted Granite Staters to know exactly where my priorities would lie as their representative.
Granite Staters responded to that choice. They saw it was proof that I was serious about changing the culture in Washington.
New Hampshire is a purple state. Every race here is competitive. And over the years, I've heard more than a few people suggest that refusing corporate PAC money meant competing with one hand tied behind my back.
But four tough congressional races later, we've shown something important: You can build a winning campaign the right way.
**I believe public service is about serving the public.**
People deserve leaders who are accountable to the communities they represent - especially in this current moment.
Now we are facing our biggest test yet: Control of the Senate could come down to New Hampshire, and Republicans and their allies are spending millions of dollars to flip this seat.
[DONATE](https://substack.com/redirect/a605042c-bece-4b3d-99df-2486342203c3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Far-right billionaires, dark money groups, and organizations backed by Big Oil and Big Pharma are lining up behind John Sununu because they know what's at stake.
It wasn't always easy, but I still refuse to take a dime of corporate PAC money -- because independence matters. I answer to Granite Staters, not corporate PACs.
I want the people I represent to know that my focus will always be on lowering costs, protecting Social Security and Medicare, defending access to abortion, and making sure people who work hard have the opportunity to get ahead.
People deserve leaders who tell them the truth, fight for their priorities, and remember who sent them to Washington in the first place.
That's what I've tried to do throughout my time in Congress, and it's the same approach I'll bring to the U.S. Senate.
This campaign comes down to independence and making sure Granite Staters are always put first.
**[Chip in $15 or whatever makes sense for you right now to stand with our grassroots-powered campaign and keep us competitive in the final days of this race.](https://substack.com/redirect/a605042c-bece-4b3d-99df-2486342203c3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Thank you,
Chris

clean_body: Hi, it's Chris. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more | | | Nov 1 | | | | | | | | | | | | Hi, it's Chris. We have less than 48 hours left in this campaign, and New Hampshire is on the line. John Sununu has taken the lead in the polls, thanks to over $67 million in GOP spending that's flooding the airwaves. We're running out of time to close this fundraising gap and keep the Granite State blue. When I first ran for Congress, I made the decision that I wouldn 't take a dime of corporate PAC money. Not because I thought it would make campaigns easier. And not because I believed everyone else had to make the same decision. I made that commitment because I wanted Granite Staters to know exactly where my priorities would lie as their representative. Granite Staters responded to that choice. They saw it was proof that I was serious about changing the culture in Washington. New Hampshire is a purple state. Every race here is competitive. And over the years, I've heard more than a few people suggest that refusing corporate PAC money meant competing with one hand tied behind my back. But four tough congressional races later, we've shown something important: You can build a winning campaign the right way. I believe public service is about serving the public. People deserve leaders who are accountable to the communities they represent - especially in this current moment. Now we are facing our biggest test yet: Control of the Senate could come down to New Hampshire, and Republicans and their allies are spending millions of dollars to flip this seat. Far-right billionaires, dark money groups, and organizations backed by Big Oil and Big Pharma are lining up behind John Sununu because they know what's at stake. It wasn't always easy, but I still refuse to take a dime of corporate PAC money -- because independence matters. I answer to Granite Staters, not corporate PACs. I want the people I represent to know that my focus will always be on lowering costs, protecting Social Security and Medicare, defending access to abortion, and making sure people who work hard have the opportunity to get ahead. People deserve leaders who tell them the truth, fight for their priorities, and remember who sent them to Washington in the first place. That's what I've tried to do throughout my time in Congress, and it's the same approach I'll bring to the U.S. Senate. This campaign comes down to independence and making sure Granite Staters are always put first. Thank you, Chris | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Chris Pappas PO Box 313, Manchester, NH 03105 ? ?
